clue.text: Robert, officer involved in ringing the changes?

parts.note: Bob is the usual short form of the name Robert
a major is an army officer ranking above a captain

explanation.surface: A man called Robert, an army officer, is caught up in some change or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing the changes' is taken literally: change ringing is the art of ringing church bells in set sequences, and the question mark flags that this is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Major is a named method of change ringing on eight church bells, so it is one pattern used when bell-ringers ring the changes.

clue.text: Frank, I'd heard, is aware of what's involved

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid, plain-spoken

indicators.note: heard tells us the word I'd is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the contraction I'd is pronounced like the word for watched or looked at

explanation.surface: Someone says they heard that a person named Frank knows what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but supplies a synonym for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Going into something with eyes wide, fully conscious of the risks, is the idiom; it means knowing what you are getting into.

clue.text: Succeed in shifting man with rake, smoker, after early finish

indicators.note: shifting means the letters are moved around into a new order
a word that finishes early has lost its final letter, so the last letter of smoker is dropped

explanation.surface: A man wielding a rake while a smoker stops early sounds like a gardening scene, but it is about achieving success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after early finish' means the smoker stops a letter short; the comma makes 'smoker' look like a third person in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave your mark is an idiom for becoming successful or making a lasting impression in some field.

clue.text: Roman Catholic is involved with transporting jute

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled, and transporting suggests carrying letters elsewhere, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Catholic is busy shipping bales of jute fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jesuit is a member of the Society of Jesus, a religious order of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Runs a contest

definitions.meaning: to run fast; the verb is given here in its third-person form

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: as a verb it means running at speed, and as a noun it means a competition to be fastest.

clue.text: Not in aberration uprooting trees

indicators.note: uprooting suggests pulling things up and scattering them, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not here means without, so the following word in is removed

explanation.surface: Pulling up trees is called an aberration, a departure from the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in' removes I and N from ABERRATION, leaving ABERRATO, whose letters are then rearranged by 'uprooting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreta (plural of arboretum) are botanical gardens devoted to trees, so the word can stand for collections of trees.

clue.text: Player to be successful with force

parts.note: to win is to be successful in a contest
g is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A sportsman needs strength to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, rugby and hockey a wing is a player positioned on the side of the field.

clue.text: 5 down tyres can burst

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A competitive event where tyres may pop.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 down' points to that clue's answer, RACE, used in its sense of lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Race in the sense of one's people or family line is a synonym for lineage and descent.

clue.text: One getting support, Italian agreement about process of wearing down

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one
a bra is an undergarment that gives support
si is the Italian word for yes
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone with backing reaches an Italian accord on erosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasion is the gradual scraping or rubbing away of a surface, erosion by friction.

clue.text: Reportedly low on power for some time

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we need a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: weak means lacking strength or power

explanation.surface: A battery or engine has been underpowered for a while, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-day period is a stretch of time, so it is one example of some time.

clue.text: Something fragrant in water from French Rhineland city

parts.note: eau is the French word for water
de is French for from
Cologne (Köln) is a city on the Rhine in Germany

explanation.surface: A perfume comes in water from a city in the Rhineland.
explanation.definitionFit: This light perfume, first made in Cologne, is a scented toilet water, so it is a fragrant product.

clue.text: On a roll, Dutch worker produces too much

parts.note: over can mean on, as in a cover laid over or on something
a bun is a small bread roll
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A Dutch employee on a winning streak is wildly productive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a roll' reads as an idiom for a streak of success, but splits into ON, A and ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Overabundant means existing in excessive quantity, more than is needed.

clue.text: No end of ballyhoo, no nervous reaction that's sleep-inducing

indicators.note: no end of means without its final letter, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: ballyhoo and hype both mean noisy publicity
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a nervous reaction

explanation.surface: Without endless fuss and no jitters, something might send you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of' but here means losing the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic describes a drug or rhythm that brings on sleep; it is a synonym for soporific.

clue.text: Ask for single shellfish to be brought round

indicators.note: the shellfish is brought round the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a clam is a bivalve shellfish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A diner orders one shellfish to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim is to demand or request something as one's due.

clue.text: They go off dramatically

parts.note: the stage direction in a script telling several actors to leave

explanation.surface: A group storms off in a theatrical huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatically' looks like 'with a flourish' but means in a play script.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word for 'they leave' is the stage direction for several characters departing.

clue.text: Day in Rome that is incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A Roman day is described as unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides was the 15th or 13th of the month, a named day.

clue.text: Abusive where one could be sailing

definitions.meaning: rude, disrespectful and offensive in speech
the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, a famous sailing water

explanation.surface: Someone out on the water turns rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rudely disrespectful, close to abusive; split in two it places a boat on a well-known English stretch of water.

clue.text: Public library has a gazetteer back in shopping centre

indicators.note: back means the following piece is read in reverse

parts.note: an A to Z is a street atlas or gazetteer, abbreviated AZ

explanation.surface: A library holds a gazetteer at the back, in a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square, and by extension a shopping precinct or mall.

clue.text: Distressingly poignant at the seaside

indicators.note: distressingly suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad scene on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Paignton is a seaside resort town in Devon in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devon town sits on the coast of Tor Bay, so it is a place found at the seaside.

clue.text: Non-commissioned officer left unpleasantly ingratiating force

indicators.note: left means departed, so the officer's letters are taken away

parts.note: smarmy means oily and ingratiating
SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major

explanation.surface: A sergeant walks out on an oily, fawning military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a military fighting force, as in the armed forces.

clue.text: Male said to have grumbled

parts.note: uttered means said or spoken

explanation.surface: A man is reported to have complained.
explanation.definitionFit: Muttered means complained in a low voice, which is what grumbling is.

clue.text: Remote in South America, island expedition

parts.note: far means distant or remote

explanation.surface: An expedition to a far-flung island off South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland trip, especially in Africa, to see or hunt animals, so it is a kind of expedition.

clue.text: Fly doctors to the capital

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, so MOS are doctors
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: Doctors fly to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is a small two-winged insect, so it is one kind of fly.

clue.text: Get old hat and conduct to the door

parts.note: to get a joke is to see it, understand it
out means out of fashion, as old hat things are

explanation.surface: A host fetches an old hat and shows a guest out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get old' looks like 'age', but 'old hat' is one phrase for unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To see someone out is to accompany a departing visitor to the exit.

clue.text: In appearance, a teacher is thinking about the future

parts.note: looking means in appearance, as in good-looking
a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher who appears to be planning ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking ahead is an idiom for considering or planning for what is to come.

clue.text: Penny left Bess' partner at drunken party

indicators.note: left means departed, so the penny letter goes

parts.note: Porgy is Bess's lover in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: Penny walked out on Bess's partner at a boozy party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party marked by excessive drinking and indulgence.

clue.text: Steamy lotion infiltrated by chemical

indicators.note: the words are infiltrated by the answer, which lies hidden across them

explanation.surface: A steamy skin cream has had a chemical slipped into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amyl is a chemical radical, and the name is short for amyl nitrite, a drug.

clue.text: A sort of smile that's crooked

parts.note: a wry smile is a twisted, mocking one

explanation.surface: A lopsided smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means askew, turned or twisted out of position.

clue.text: Worthless weapon returned by amateur, one on the right

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: An amateur gives back a useless weapon to a right-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, futile.

clue.text: Play room

definitions.meaning: play here is slack or freedom of movement, as in a loose joint
room here is scope or freedom to act

explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom from restriction; both play and room describe that space to move.
